symbols.name: fractional places
symbols.meaning: The number of fractional binary places kept by truncation, a count of binary digits after the point.
symbols.quote: Let $p$ be the number of fractional binary places kept, so the grid spacing is $2^{-p}$.

symbols.name: truncation operator
symbols.meaning: The map that truncates each real and imaginary part of every coefficient of a list toward zero onto the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb{Z}$.
symbols.quote: Then $Q_p w$ is the list obtained by truncating each real and imaginary part of each coefficient toward zero onto the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb{Z}$, where $\mathbb{Z}$ is the set of [integers](integer.md).

symbols.name: coefficient list
symbols.meaning: A finite list of complex numbers, called coefficients, to which truncation is applied.
symbols.quote: Let $w$ be a finite list of complex numbers, called coefficients.

symbols.name: integers
symbols.quote: Then $Q_p w$ is the list obtained by truncating each real and imaginary part of each coefficient toward zero onto the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb{Z}$, where $\mathbb{Z}$ is the set of [integers](integer.md).

symbols.name: array norm
symbols.meaning: The largest complex modulus of any coefficient of an array.
symbols.quote: The error is measured by the [Array norm](array-norm.md) $\|\cdot\|_\infty$, the largest complex modulus of any coefficient, where the modulus of $a+bi$ is $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$.

symbols.name: layer
symbols.meaning: The map that performs one layer, replacing each selected pair of entries by their half-sum and half-difference.
symbols.quote: A layer, written $H$, is one pass over the list.

symbols.name: first pair value
symbols.meaning: The value of the first entry in a pair of entries combined by a layer.
symbols.quote: For every pair of entries whose [addresses](address.md) differ in one of several selected bits, with values $s$ and $r$, it replaces the pair by $((s+r)/2,(s-r)/2)$.

symbols.name: second pair value
symbols.meaning: The value of the second entry in a pair of entries combined by a layer.
symbols.quote: For every pair of entries whose [addresses](address.md) differ in one of several selected bits, with values $s$ and $r$, it replaces the pair by $((s+r)/2,(s-r)/2)$.

relations.predicate: is taken over pairs chosen by
relations.quote: Truncation is taken over pairs chosen by their [addresses](address.md), with one rounding per layer.
